previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and a history of anxiety and depression was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She was found to be in diabetic ketoacidosis with acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration. She was treated with IV fluids and insulin, and her metabolic abnormalities improved. A central line was placed for access, which later led to an iatrogenic pneumothorax requiring a pigtail catheter for drainage. The lung re-expanded successfully, and the chest tube was removed before discharge. H. pylori infection was diagnosed and treated with antibiotics. Her mental health concerns were acknowledged, and she was discharged home with a plan for follow-up on her diabetes, kidney function, esophageal varices, and psychiatric care.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with type I DM that has been difficult to control c/b by 
retinopathy, nephropathy, and likely gastroparesis who presents 
with N/V, similar to previous episodes, c/w severe anxiety with 
likely gastroparesis flare.

# Abdominal pain, nausea: Appeared consistent with prior 
gastroparesis flares triggered by back pain and anxiety 
surrounding this. KUB showed no concerning abnormalities.  Pain, 
nausea, anorexia resolved with dilaudid in ED. Patient had been 
eating since admission and was tolerating PO food, but continued 
to have some nausea.  We gradually advanced her diet, and 
transitioned pain control to her home regimen, minimizing 
additional narcotics.  We also controlled her nausea with ativan 
and ondansetron, and continued her home dose PPI.  

# Hypertension: She was hypertensive on presentation to the 
floor, but this improved improved with a single dose of home 
dose lisinopril, which she had been unable to tolerate PO prior 
to pain control. Based on prior notes, her hypertension and 
tachycardia (see below) seem to occur secondary to high 
sympathetic tone due to pain and anxiety.  However, given 
persistently elevated creatinine above baseline, we subsequently 
stopped lisinopril, and started her on amlodipine instead.  

# DM type I: Last A1c improved to 9.3 in ___, perhaps 
because of improved compliance with BID 70/30. Significant 
glucosuria and proteinuria on UA. No evidence of ketoacidosis.  
We hydrated her with IV fluids, continued diabetic diet and home 
70/30 insulin with a qachs humalog insulin sliding scale.  UA 
did not show any evidence of ketoacidosis.  Elevated creatinine 
despite hydration may be an indicator of advancing diabetic 
nephropathy, and we have communicated with PCP office to arrange 
outpatient followup with nephrology as soon as possible, in 
addition to discontinuing ACE inhibitor and starting amlodipine 
for BP control.

# ___: Creatinine up to 2.0 from normal baseline. Likely ___ 
dehydration in the setting of poor PO intake.  Creatinine 
trended down to 1.8 during admission with hydration, but did not 
improve further, causing concern for a component of advancing 
diabetic nephropathy.  We swtiched her ACE inhibitor to 
amlodipine, and have communicated with PCP office to arrange 
urgent renal outpatient followup.

# Sinus tachycardia: Likely related to sympathetic tone due to 
pain, anxiety, and also some hypovolemia.  This improved 
somewhat with IV hydration and resumption of PO diet.

# Depression with psychotic features:  We continued risperidone 
and ativan
